what: Iran begins public mourning for Ayatollah killed in February

clean_source_blocks.text: Iran has begun several days of public mourning and funeral processions for its former Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, more than four months after he was killed in strikes launched by the US and Israel. The former Ayatollah's body will lie in state in Tehran's Grand Mosalla from Friday, ahead of his burial in his hometown of Mashhad next Thursday. Officials have said the funeral could draw up to 20 million mourners from across Iran, according to AFP. It comes as Iran and the United States observe a fragile ceasefire after signing a preliminary deal to halt their conflict in June. Khamenei's body will lie in the Grand Mosalla for three days, alongside the remains of family members who were also killed in the US and Israeli strikes in February.

Iran's ruling clerics are preparing days of mass funeral rites for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei as a show of public devotion to the Islamic Republic and proof that its revolutionary fervour still burns strong. The supreme leader ‌was killed on the ‌first day of Israeli and US air strikes against Iran on February 28 and the funeral events will begin on Saturday in Tehran, with mass processions planned next week in Qom and Mashhad and ceremonies in Iraq. Tehran is preparing a massive security operation for the funeral. "The large public turnout ‌at the funeral procession of the martyred leader and the other martyrs will, in effect, be another referendum for the Islamic Republic," Qom Friday prayer leader Ayatollah Mohammad Saidi declared to state media.
Ali Khamenei's body will lie in state in Tehran's Grand Mosalla from Friday ahead of days-long funeral events.

There will be an official funeral ceremony in Tehran on Saturday. Authorities have ordered public and private offices in Tehran to close from Saturday through Monday, while traffic restrictions will shut down most of the city centre to private vehicles, AFP reported. The airspace over Tehran will be partially closed from Friday and fully closed on Monday. Following the ceremonies in Tehran, the former supreme leader's body will be taken to the Iraqi holy cities of Najaf and Karbala, prior to his burial in Mashhad. Representatives from multiple countries are expected to attend the ceremonies, including Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. Khamenei was succeeded by his son, Mojtaba, who has not been seen in public since becoming supreme leader. Who is Mojtaba Khamenei, Iran's new supreme leader? Ayatollah Khamenei's iron grip on power in Iran comes to an end ---

[Lähde: BBC]
Iran has begun several days of public mourning and funeral processions for its former Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, more than four months after he was killed in strikes launched by the US and Israel.

The former Ayatollah's body will lie in state in Tehran's Grand Mosalla from Friday, ahead of his burial in his hometown of Mashhad next Thursday.

Officials have said the funeral could draw up to 20 million mourners from across Iran, according to AFP.

It comes as Iran and the United States observe a fragile ceasefire after signing a preliminary deal to halt their conflict in June.

Khamenei's body will lie in the Grand Mosalla for three days, alongside the remains of family members who were also killed in the US and Israeli strikes in February.

There will be an official funeral ceremony in Tehran on Saturday.

Authorities have ordered public and private offices in Tehran to close from Saturday through Monday, while traffic restrictions will shut down most of the city centre to private vehicles, AFP reported. The airspace over Tehran will be partially closed from Friday and fully closed on Monday.

Following the ceremonies in Tehran, the former supreme leader's body will be taken to the Iraqi holy cities of Najaf and Karbala, prior to his burial in Mashhad.

Representatives from multiple countries are expected to attend the ceremonies, including Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

Khamenei was succeeded by his son, Mojtaba, who has not been seen in public since becoming supreme leader.

---

[Lähde: Newcastle Herald]
Iran's ruling clerics are preparing days of mass funeral rites for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei as a show of public devotion to the Islamic Republic and proof that its revolutionary fervour still burns strong.

The supreme leader ‌was killed on the ‌first day of Israeli and US air strikes against Iran on February 28 and the funeral events will begin on Saturday in Tehran, with mass processions planned next week in Qom and Mashhad and ceremonies in Iraq.

Tehran is preparing a massive security operation for the funeral.

"The large public turnout ‌at the funeral procession of the martyred leader and the other martyrs will, in effect, be another referendum for the Islamic Republic," Qom Friday prayer leader Ayatollah Mohammad Saidi declared to state media.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian expressed profound sorrow over Khamenei's death but emphasised national fortitude, urging citizens of all backgrounds to join the procession to present a unified front to the global community.

In a statement,  Pezeshkian said: "This martyrdom is not the end of the journey, but the beginning of a new chapter of national unity, resilience, and progress," pointing out that "this system rests on the firm foundations of faith, ideals, and the will of a great nation."

In Iran's theocratic system, Khamenei was ‌not only head of state and ​leader of a revolutionary movement, but the representative for Shi'ite Islam's 12th imam who disappeared in the ninth century.

Khamenei's death in an enemy attack plays into a powerful Shi'ite tradition of martyrdom and mourning, in which processions of black-clad flagellants beat ​their chests or backs during ‌annual religious commemorations.

That potent symbolism has been evident in the black funeral flags hanging over city streets since his death and in mourning ceremonies for him referencing the martyrdom of Shi'ism's third imam, Hossein.

Workers were stringing up ​new posters in Tehran proclaiming support for the new leader Mojtaba, with the images of the late Khamenei and a raised revolutionary fist behind him.

For supporters of the Islamic Republic, the talk of martyrdom is no mere rhetoric.

"These are the hardest days of my life," said Mohsen, 24, a Basij member in Tehran who asked not to give his family name.

"I do not remember the time when Imam Khomeini passed away but my father says the entire country ​was ​engulfed in grief and mourning. Today, too, people are in mourning, especially because our leader was martyred," he ​added.

payload.title: Iran aloitti julkisen suruajan ajatollah Ali Khamenein kuoleman jälkeen
payload.summary: Iranissa on alkanut useita päiviä kestävä julkinen suruaika ja hautajaistapahtumien sarja entisen korkeimman johtajan ajatollah Ali Khamenein kuoleman jälkeen.
payload.content:
Iranissa on alkanut useita päiviä kestävä julkinen suruaika entisen korkeimman johtajan ajatollah Ali Khamenein kuoleman jälkeen. Khamenei kuoli helmikuun 28. päivänä Yhdysvaltain ja Israelin Irania vastaan tekemien ilmaiskujen ensimmäisenä päivänä. Hänen ruumiinsa asetetaan nähtäville Teheranin Grand Mosallaan perjantaista alkaen ennen virallista hautajaisseremoniaa ja myöhempää hautausta Mashhadissa.

## Hautajaisista odotetaan laajoja

Khamenein ruumis on määrä pitää Grand Mosallassa kolmen päivän ajan. Samassa yhteydessä nähtäville asetetaan myös helmikuun iskuissa kuolleiden perheenjäsenten jäännöksiä. Virallinen hautajaisseremonia järjestetään Teheranissa lauantaina.

Iranin viranomaiset ovat arvioineet, että surutilaisuudet voivat kerätä eri puolilta maata jopa 20 miljoonaa osallistujaa. Ensi viikolle on suunniteltu joukkohautajaiskulkueita myös Qomissa ja Mashhadissa, ja seremonioita järjestetään lisäksi Irakissa. Teheranin tilaisuuksien jälkeen Khamenein ruumis viedään Irakin pyhiin kaupunkeihin Najafiin ja Karbalaan ennen hautausta hänen kotikaupungissaan Mashhadissa ensi torstaina.

Useiden maiden edustajien odotetaan osallistuvan seremonioihin. Osallistujien joukossa on määrä olla Pakistanin pääministeri Shehbaz Sharif.

## Teheran sulkee toimistoja ja rajoittaa liikennettä

Hautajaisjärjestelyihin liittyy Teheranissa laaja turvallisuusoperaatio. Viranomaiset ovat määränneet kaupungin julkiset ja yksityiset toimistot suljettaviksi lauantaista maanantaihin. Lisäksi liikennejärjestelyt sulkevat suurimman osan keskustasta yksityisautoilta.

Teheranin ilmatila suljetaan osittain perjantaista alkaen ja kokonaan maanantaina. Toimet kertovat siitä, kuinka suurena poliittisena ja turvallisuuteen liittyvänä tapahtumana Iranin johto hautajaisia pitää.

Iranin hallitsevat papit ovat kuvanneet hautajaisia myös uskollisuuden osoituksena islamilaiselle tasavallalle. Qomin perjantairukouksen johtaja ajatollah Mohammad Saidi sanoi valtiolliselle medialle, että suuri osallistujamäärä olisi käytännössä uusi kansanäänestys islamilaiselle tasavallalle.

Suruajan taustalla Iran ja Yhdysvallat noudattavat haurasta tulitaukoa sen jälkeen, kun maat allekirjoittivat kesäkuussa alustavan sopimuksen konfliktinsa pysäyttämiseksi. Khamenein seuraajaksi on noussut hänen poikansa Mojtaba Khamenei, jota ei ole nähty julkisuudessa korkeimman johtajan tehtävään nousemisen jälkeen.

Khamenein ruumis asetetaan nähtäville Teheranissa ennen hautausta Mashhadissa ensi torstaina.
Viranomaiset ovat määränneet Teheraniin sulkuja, liikennerajoituksia ja ilmatilan rajoituksia hautajaisten ajaksi.

Iran has begun several days of public mourning and funeral processions for its former Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, more than four months after he was killed in strikes launched by the US and Israel. The former Ayatollah's body will lie in state in Tehran's Grand Mosalla from Friday, ahead of his burial in his hometown of Mashhad next Thursday. Officials have said the funeral could draw up to 20 million mourners from across Iran, according to AFP. It comes as Iran and the United States observe a fragile ceasefire after signing a preliminary deal to halt their conflict in June. Khamenei's body will lie in the Grand Mosalla for three days, alongside the remains of family members who were also killed in the US and Israeli strikes in February.

Iran's ruling clerics are preparing days of mass funeral rites for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei as a show of public devotion to the Islamic Republic and proof that its revolutionary fervour still burns strong. The supreme leader ‌was killed on the ‌first day of Israeli and US air strikes against Iran on February 28 and the funeral events will begin on Saturday in Tehran, with mass processions planned next week in Qom and Mashhad and ceremonies in Iraq. Tehran is preparing a massive security operation for the funeral. "The large public turnout ‌at the funeral procession of the martyred leader and the other martyrs will, in effect, be another referendum for the Islamic Republic," Qom Friday prayer leader Ayatollah Mohammad Saidi declared to state media.

Ali Khamenei's body will lie in state in Tehran's Grand Mosalla from Friday ahead of days-long funeral events.

There will be an official funeral ceremony in Tehran on Saturday. Authorities have ordered public and private offices in Tehran to close from Saturday through Monday, while traffic restrictions will shut down most of the city centre to private vehicles, AFP reported. The airspace over Tehran will be partially closed from Friday and fully closed on Monday. Following the ceremonies in Tehran, the former supreme leader's body will be taken to the Iraqi holy cities of Najaf and Karbala, prior to his burial in Mashhad. Representatives from multiple countries are expected to attend the ceremonies, including Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. Khamenei was succeeded by his son, Mojtaba, who has not been seen in public since becoming supreme leader. Who is Mojtaba Khamenei, Iran's new supreme leader? Ayatollah Khamenei's iron grip on power in Iran comes to an end ---
